So, VPN's are not magic. The only thing they do is disassociate your IP with your location and identity.

The problem that a lot of people seem to ignore is that while the VPN does obfuscate their identity, they still use the same computer to access both their ISP's network and their VPN's network. Why is that important? Well your computer with all it's little applications that phone home identify you. Most applications these days create some form of unique identifier and in most cases have your personal identity recorded to some extent. When they phone home those companies know exactly who you are. And now they know that you're using a VPN.

An analogy would be like driving your car to work. Every day you take the same route. Then one day you decide to obfuscate your route to work by taking another route you've never been down. But you're still driving the same car with the same license plate. That's not exactly anonymous, is it?

You've also got to worry about DNS leaks and the times your VPN disconnects reconnecting you to your ISP's network while you're in the middle of doing all those things you want to hide. In those cases even if you used another computer with no identifying applications installed your cover is blown and you have to start over with a new computer because any software you install is capable and very likely using your CPU's unique identifier to create its own identifier. If it's an OS like IOS, MacOS, Windows and Ubuntu, they're phoning home and identifying you all the time.

I always found it odd that most VPN's out of the box don't make the capabilities to prevent DNS leaks and prevent reconnects to your ISP's network during disconnects easy to implement when it is easy to implement but somewhat obfuscated and technical.
